sections.content:
Same Prof as ELEC 2100, Prof MIAO Wenchao is responsible for this course in this semester.

Content:
L1: Boolean algebra basics (De Morgan's Law, K-map)
L2: Combinational logic (1) - Simple Logic Gates
L3: Combinational logic (2) - Multiplexer & Demultiplexers
L4: Combinational logic (3) - Full Adder Design
L5: Sequential logic (1) - Flip-flop basics, timing diagram
L6: Sequential logic (2) - Finite-state Machine and counters
L7: Sequential logic (3) - Finite-state Machine Design with examples
L8: Sequential logic (4) - Reverse engineer FSMs
L9: Sequential logic (5) - FSM Registers
L10: FSM Counters
L11: FSM Implementation with FFs, Latches on an FPGA
L12: Inside logic gates (NMOS, PMOS transistors)
L13: FSM Examples (for training)

See this course as a two-parted course, first half is about combinational logic circuits, the AND, OR, NOR, NAND goodies

the second half is about Flip-flops and Finite state machines, here where the real stuff comes.

Lab tasks are about:
In Vivado, use VHDL to write series of code to control your Xilinx FPGA board, and make desired output.

I will not talk about the miniproject here, I want you to feel the project by yourself.

Suggestions, if you wanna prepare this course:

- Karnaugh Map (K-map)
This course has minimum-to-no mention of K-map, except lightly touching the concept at the very beginning of the semester. Then suddenly in FSM counters (L10), you are REQUIRED to know how to solve a 4-variable K-map.

- The ability to fill in a truth table in an efficient manner
This course has a very tight midterm and final exam time limit, be sure to know how to fill in the truth table quickly.

Lab task suggestions:

- Spare at least 2-3 days before your lab to at least finish part of your lab, in lab 5 and 6, you may need more time, more on that in the "workload" part.

- Prepare Vivado before you start your first lab task, don't wait until the last minute.

- Be mindful that Vivado is buggy and may throw weird exception to you.
sections.teaching:
In case you're interested why TANG TANG has a surname like that, he said he's Spanish and coincidentally his father and mother has the same surname, he's named therefore.

TANG TANG is a fun guy that tell jokes from time to time in tutorials, so full of fun to attend his class.
sections.workload:
As you can see, this course is a project course, with emphasis on the labs and projects rather than the exams, most of your pain will come from the labs and project.

You're required to find a lab partner at the first week of lab session, and you're stick to them throughout the course. They are also the one who will work with you during the project.

Content of the labs:
-- combinational circuit --
Lab 1: Controlling LED (cancelled due to typhoon)
Lab 2: XOR gate array and full adder
Lab 3: 4-bit full adder
Lab 4: 4-bit full adder/subtractor (with overflow detection)
-- sequential circuit starts --
Lab 5: 4-bit up counter
Lab 6: 4-bit adder/subtractor with display

For most of the labs, you would see VHDL skeleton code and guide, so no big worries if you work ahead.

Do be mindful of the steps of creating a Vivado Project, I believe you can find some ways to cut corners, right?

Taking the project into account, the workload is mild to heavy, especially during the last few weeks, be sure to work early, you need your time to fix your timing errors.

sections.content:
The content is about a lot of digital logic including
boolean algebra
combinational logic
sequential logic
finite state machine

Those combinational logic have been covered in ELEC 1100 before, and although sequetial logic is more challenging than combinational logic, it is still simple.
sections.teaching:
I think Prof YOBAS teach very well. He will provide a lot of take home exericse that can improve your understaning in digital logic. Also
explain very well in every topic no matter the topic were covered in ELEC1100 or not. Moreover, Prof YOBAS will answer every question you ask after or in the lecture. Teaching team will also prepare some assignment and exercise before mid term will be provide for us to prepare for the mid term exam.
About the TA, for the tutorial, Ray explain every tutorial question very deep, and Ray is a very nice person that will interact with student in the turtorial, keep tracking what you are currently doing. (So don't sleep in his lesson :D)
But in my observation, most of the student skip all the lecture and tutorial and only attend the lab session that contribute in grading :(
sections.grading:
I believe the grading would be good, I will update the grading part after I received the grade.

mid term:
Full marks=100
Max = 94
Min =3
Mean=55.31
Median=56
Stdev=20.10

And I got a 94/100, and getting full mark is possible, this is a very good course
sections.workload:
In the teaching part I stated that some exercise and assignment was released before the mid term exam, and those exercise and assignment doesn't affect on grading, but strongly recommend you to do those exercise) So don't worry on the workload.
The only things that contribute in the grading other than mid term and final exam is the lab session. If you miss any one of the lab session you will directly receive a F.
You will totally only have 4 HW that doesn't contribute in grading.
6 lab, one project
one mid term exam
and one final exam only

sections.content: The main topics of this course are combinational logic, sequential logic and the most important one, Finite State Machine (FSM). For combinational logic, it will be pretty easy if you have studied other related courses before. It also requires you to apply the knowledge in this course to implement the VHDL codes into the FPGA board.
sections.teaching:
Professor Yobas explains everything in detail and sometimes lets us apply the lecture content just taught to answer the questions.

TA Tang Tang is good as well. He clearly explains the details in the tutorials, which are the introductions for the following labs. The code examples are given so we have a better image of completing the labs.
sections.grading:
Midterm 25% (60/100)
Final 25% (48/100)
7 Labs 25% (521/530)
Mini Project 15% (100/100)
Participation 10% (Not shown, but maybe 8%-10%)
Homework 0% (If your mark is marginal and you have done all 5 pieces of homework, one grade can be up.)

Only labs and the project have the requirement of full attendance.

Overall 75.3%-77.3%
Grade: B-
I expect my grade will be C/C+ but because I submitted all the homework on time.
sections.workload:
Usually one lab every week
The skeleton codes are usually given in the lab manuals and it will be easy to fill in the remaining parts if you understand the concepts in the lecture and tutorial notes.

Homework consists of 1-3 questions and it will be easy if you understand the concepts in lectures.

sections.content:
There are mainly three topics in this course

1. Combinational logic(and, or, xor... all the gate)
2. Sequential Logic
3. FSM(Finite State Machines) and almost half of the course is about this

This course is not hard at all if your logical skill is good enough.
sections.teaching:
Although I mention the course not being hard, professor explain almost every single concept to you in the lecture, which makes the course a little bit boring when you understand how it works.

Tutorials are all about labs and the mini project. The labs are about VHDL coding, which is about programming a Basys 3 board. The progress and the result is different compared with software programming like C++ and  Python, etc. But the coding part is easy if you already complete COMP2011 or something similar.
sections.grading:
As you have to finish the lab and project to get pass, you always get full marks on that.

Homework does not count in course grade under usual situation, but I still recommend you to finish all if you are not that busy. Because the same question may appears in mid term and final exam (For me, yes).

However, getting high marks on mid term and final exam is difficult. As everyone perform pretty well, you have to pay much more attention on how to design the logical circuit and how to make it works. Deep understanding on each components is a must to get A or B+, for example like different kinds of flip-flop(D ,JK, T), Multiplexer, Decoder. Finishing homework can practice your brain on transforming different parts using gates.

Finally, there is course participation marks on course grading. According to the professor, the most easier method to get all participation marks is to attend the lecture, answer questions and ask as much as you can. Make the professor remember you.

mid: 25%, final: 25%, lab and project: 40%, Hw: 0%(usually), course participation: 10%
sections.workload:
There are 7 labs and 1 mini project (all in pair of 2) need to do in the whole course. You must finish all to pass the course. But there are skeleton code for you and the remaining part is piece of cake if you attend the tutorial or have knowledge on how to software programming. I think the most difficult part of lab is to installing Vivado (the software to finish the labs), for student this semester. We have to write Email to AMD to get the permission to install.

Total 5 homework, but it does not count in the grade if you work fine in this course. Homework will help when you fail on mid term and final exam marks. You will get pass (the course grade) if you are almost fail but with all homework done.
